note: Calls the 54/64 'kinds of pitch (by type and location)' plain 'pitch types' and drops 'above the zone' from the splitter, which could read as an in-zone middle splitter.
Says to avoid the fastball, but a letter-high fastball on the edge is the tool's third-best pitch; only letter-high changeups are listed as worst.
Says a higher chase rate means he 'takes more pitches outside the zone', but it means he swings at more of them.
Calls his fastball the hardest in the league (one pitcher throws harder), calls 4.7 km/h above average 'just above', and invents a causal link between fastball usage and in-zone rate.
Never answers who strikes out more, though the profiles show strikeout rates of 0.208 for Lee and 0.193 for Kim.
Gives walk rate as a share of at-bats, but the tool defines it per batter faced.
Says most lost strikes are fastballs, but 124 of 396 is about 31%, not a majority.
